name: Casino Swazi
description: Swazi Casino is a Royal Casino variant played in Eswatini (formerly Swaziland). Features unique building mechanics where captured cards are kept face up and top cards can be stolen by opponents for builds. Uses numerical values for picture cards (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14).

history.origins: Swazi Casino is a variant of Royal Casino played in Eswatini (formerly Swaziland), a country in Southern Africa. It was documented by Jonathan Dushoff. The game is part of a family of African Casino variants that differ from Anglo-American Casino.
timeline: Traditional: Played for generations in Eswatini
Current: Popular card game in Eswatini
history.cultural: Popular in Eswatini and neighboring regions. The game is often played socially and in family gatherings. Similar variants are played in Lesotho (Sotho Casino) and South Africa.
history.evolution: The key innovation of African Casino variants is that captured cards are kept face up, and opponents can use the top card of your capture pile in their builds. This creates complex tactical considerations about when to capture.

setup.players: 2-4 players. 4 players play in fixed partnerships (partners opposite). Play is anticlockwise.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Card values: 2-10=face value, J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1 or 14. All picture cards have numerical values (Royal Casino style).
setup.dealing: Player to dealer's right cuts 4 cards from middle of deck to form initial layout. Dealer deals all cards to players one at a time. First dealer random; deal passes right. If initial layout has 3+ points in scoring cards or 3+ picture cards, reshuffle and recut.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the layout. First player/team to reach target score (usually 11 or 21 points) wins.
rules.gameplay: Captured cards kept face up in single pile. New captures on top. Capturing card must be on top. You can sort captured cards but opponents don't see the order. Partners share a pile in 4-player game. Layout: 4 initial cards, can be captured or added to. Builds: Single build (sum=value) or Augmented build (multiple sets with same value). Build owner must capture it eventually. Turn: Must play exactly one card from hand. Actions (in any order, before/after playing): 1) Capture (chow) - play card to capture matching card(s) or builds, 2) Create single build, 3) Change build value, 4) Create/add to augmented build, 5) Discard to layout. Can only do one of actions 1/3/5 per turn (involve playing card). Can do multiple of actions 2/4 without playing card. Cannot capture directly from opponent's pile, but can use top card in augmented builds. Drifting: Playing a card that could capture but using it in build instead - legal but opponents can insist on capture if you try to leave capturable cards. Capturing card must go on top of pile.

strategy.basic: Capture cards when you can. Build when you have the capturing card. Be careful about capturing early - your pile becomes available to opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Tactics center on builds, especially high-value builds. If you have a monopoly on aces (value 14), build 14s that opponents cannot touch. Time your captures carefully - early capture gives opponents access to your top card.
strategy.advanced: Complex build strategies: create rival piles (e.g., building 14s vs opponent's 12s). High-value builds are powerful because they're easy to augment. Don't release Q, K, A early if it gives opponent monopoly. Use drifting to signal partner. Consider that capturing a 10 or 2 gives opponents access to valuable cards.
